dataflow.outcome: stale normalization binding, false provenance tuple, and missing or skipped enrichment
dataflow.sink: tree entry `raw_hash` plus attached `NormalizeRef` and rebuild `load_normalized_units()` lookup
dataflow.source: working-file bytes controlled by a local or synced scope contributor
dataflow.summary: candidate bytes -> verified normalization -> path-keyed `NormalizeRef` -> closing snapshot reread -> tree entry -> rebuild unit lookup

impact.why: The issue crosses the local provenance boundary and can make historical metadata and enrichment inconsistent for changed files.

likelihood.why: The interleaving is realistic for shared or synced content, but deterministic scheduling frequency was not measured.

limitations: The finding does not demonstrate code execution, credential exposure, or arbitrary file access.
Normalized units remain keyed by raw hash, limiting the consequence to false provenance and missing/skipped enrichment.

reachability.entrypoint: file modification during the index-to-auto-snapshot interval
reachability.outcome: local archive/search provenance integrity degradation for affected files
reachability.summary: The attacker needs concurrent modification access to the selected scope and timing during a normal local `kcs index` run; there is no network listener.

attackPath.summary: A lower-trust local or synced-folder contributor changes a selected file after KCS normalizes the old bytes but before the closing snapshot rereads the path. The published tree entry then names the new bytes and carries a normalization reference for old bytes, causing false historical metadata and missing or skipped enrichment on rebuild.

codeEvidence.explanation: `kcs index` carries the result of normalization directly into the automatic snapshot as `normalize_by_path`, so any identity metadata omitted from that map is unavailable at publication time.
codeEvidence.label: Index passes path-keyed normalization map into auto snapshot

codeEvidence.explanation: `NormalizeRef` records profile and generation but not the expected raw hash, while `TreeEntry` stores `raw_hash` separately. The publication path must therefore verify compatibility before attaching the reference.
codeEvidence.label: NormalizeRef does not carry the raw hash it was produced for

codeEvidence.explanation: The earlier interval is protected: KCS normalizes only bytes whose current hash still matches the scan-time hash. The missing control is not here; it is the later loss of this verified `raw_hash` when publishing the snapshot.
codeEvidence.label: Candidate bytes are rehashed before normalization

codeEvidence.explanation: After normalization, the pipeline stores only `candidate.input_path -> NormalizeRef`. The verified `raw_hash` is no longer carried with the pending publication metadata.
codeEvidence.label: Successful normalization is downgraded to a path-keyed reference

codeEvidence.explanation: The snapshot computes `raw_hash` from the current bytes, then copies any path-matching `NormalizeRef` into the tree entry without checking that the reference was produced for that same raw hash.
codeEvidence.label: Closing snapshot rereads bytes and attaches by path only

codeEvidence.explanation: A later rebuild records the tree entry raw hash with the attached profile/generation and attempts to load units for that tuple. If the bytes changed after normalization, the tuple names new bytes with old-byte metadata.
codeEvidence.label: Rebuild consumes the tree raw hash with the attached reference

confidence: high (0.97) for the static interleaving; medium for occurrence frequency

regression_tests: Unchanged bytes attach the normalization reference as before.
Bytes changed after normalization do not attach the reference and emit a visible event or retry signal.
Rebuild does not create a `tree_entries` row that pairs the changed raw hash with the old profile/generation.
remediation.summary: Carry the expected normalized raw hash with each pending path mapping and attach `NormalizeRef` only if the closing snapshot reads the same raw hash. On mismatch, skip attachment, log a visible drift event, or abort/retry the snapshot according to product policy.

rootCause.summary: The violated invariant is that a `NormalizeRef` may be attached to a tree entry only for the raw bytes that were normalized. KCS protects the scan-to-normalize interval, but it loses the verified raw hash when it stores `candidate.input_path -> NormalizeRef`; the closing snapshot then binds that old reference to whatever bytes are present at the same path.

summary: The `kcs index` pipeline verifies bytes before normalization, but then records only a path-keyed `NormalizeRef`. The automatic closing snapshot rereads current file bytes and attaches that reference by path without comparing the raw hash that was normalized, allowing a concurrent local file change to publish a tree entry whose `raw_hash` names new bytes while its normalization metadata was produced for old bytes.
title: closing snapshot can attach normalization metadata to different bytes

assertions: The earlier scan-to-normalize guard is correct and does not bind the later snapshot publication.
The closing snapshot attaches by file name after computing the current raw hash.
Rebuild consumes the tree raw hash with the attached profile and generation.
limitations: No scheduler-controlled race was run inside KCS.
No downstream escalation beyond local provenance/enrichment integrity was demonstrated.
validation.method: static source trace plus synthetic local regression probe
validation.summary: The saved validation traced the verified old bytes through normalization, the path-keyed reference, the closing reread of current bytes, and rebuild consumption. The included synthetic probe confirms that path-only attachment can produce a tree entry with a new raw hash and a stale reference, while an `expected_raw_hash` check rejects the drift.
